jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Reporting into the General Manager, the Director, Finance will partner with various functions of our business, providing timely financial insights in a collaborative environment. The Director, Finance will have direct influence and impact on the strategic financial decisions within the business unit, including pricing, new product feasibility, ongoing project profitability, quarterly forecasting, customer profitability and management reporting. This role leads a team of 2-3 direct reports, providing mentorship, direction and day-to-day leadership for the finance function.

This position is right for you if you are strategic, action-oriented, challenge the status quo, highly analytical, results-driven, have a high level of energy, have high attention to detail, and can communicate clearly and concisely. As a member of the leadership team, you will be highly visible, partnering with all areas of the business, you will share a passion for developing talent with a focus on building sustained long-term growth and creating a fantastic place to work.

Job Description

Minimum Base Salary:
$160,000

Maximum Base Salary:
$170,000

Responsibilities

Direct oversight of accounting operations, transactions, and internal controls (including but not limited to record to report, order to cash and procure to pay)
Oversee the month end processes, reconciliations and internal reporting to ensure accurate and timely financial reporting, including reviewing and producing period end variance reports and commentary
Maintains a documented system of accounting policies and procedures; implements a system of controls over accounting transactions to minimize risk.
Oversee the Percentage of Completion method to recognize revenue based on work performed, aligning revenue with actual costs incurred, efforts expended, or physical milestones achieved.
Accountable for accurate and timely monthly/quarterly financial reporting to ensure compliance with internal and external reporting (in accordance with IFRS)
Coordinate, analyze and present the monthly financial performance to the Executive Team, Senior Management and Modaxo
Own the quarterly financial forecasting process (“QSR”), including but not limited to: consideration of the sales pipeline, costs analysis (COGS and OPEX), and key drivers and assumptions.
Govern, with the support of the General Manger, execution of action plans from the QSR review process  
Provide leadership, guidance and coaching to direct reports, ensuring continual development, performance expectations and engagement, performance reviews and goal setting, and fostering a collaborative team environment
Lead financial analysis over any new product initiatives which would include cost assessment, revenue forecasts and overall lifetime profitability
Responsible for working with the business to assess market pricing, new deal pricing, and sales approach for our products.
Monitor and input on key metrics of individual customer contracts 
Monitor and enforce Key Performance Indicators (KPI)
Provide corporate tax support; transfer pricing, and state revenue allocations
Coordinate, analyze and report the financial performance to the Leadership Team and the Modaxo Team (Group(s) > Portfolio > Global).
Become an expert in the company’s forecasting tool, Adaptive Planning, and knowledgeable in the company’s other key tools such as OpenAir (PSA), SalesForce (CRM) and Great Plains/NetSuite (ERP).
Work closely with all functional leads to ensure projects bids and contract terms, financial and otherwise, adhere to corporate parameters

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Management or a related field.
Professional accounting designation (CPA, CMA, or CA)
Minimum of 10+ years accounting and/or finance experience, minimum 5 years in a management role within Finance

Excellent with Microsoft Excel
Experience in Adaptive Planning, OpenAir, NetSuite, PowerBI a plus
Familiarity with AI-driven automation tools (e.g., FloQast, BlackLine, or ERP AI integrations)
Ability to perform under pressure and meet deadlines

Dalhousie University is embarking on a significant transformation of its administrative services, reshaping how services are organized, delivered and enabled by technology across the institution. The multi-year Service Modernization Program will simplify and standardize processes, modernize service delivery, introduce new operating models and enterprise technologies, and strengthen the University’s ability to deliver high-quality, sustainable services for students, faculty and staff. jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), you’ll provide strategic and operational leadership for Equitable’s enterprise information security program, protecting our information assets, technology infrastructure, applications, data, and digital capabilities while enabling business growth and innovation. You’ll define and execute our cyber security strategy, ensuring effective security controls, processes, and practices are embedded across technology and business operations. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, you’ll lead the continued development of a resilient, risk-aware security culture while ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and recognized security frameworks.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

Reports To:
Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer

Department:
Information Technology

Term:
Permanent Full-Time

What you’ll do:

Serve as a senior technology leader and trusted advisor to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer and Executive Team on cyber security, significant incidents, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security program developments
Develop and execute the enterprise cyber security strategy, roadmap, budget, and investment priorities aligned with business and technology objectives, including anticipating and mitigating risks associated with AI-enabled threats and vulnerabilities
Establish and maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, controls, metrics, and performance indicators, driving continuous improvement in the organization’s security capabilities and maturity
Lead security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability management, cyber resilience, incident response, recovery, post-incident remediation, and the oversight of security service providers and critical technology assets
Oversee security architecture, identity and access management, data protection, cloud and endpoint security, ensuring appropriate controls are integrated into technology solutions, projects, and business processes
Partner with business and technology leaders to enable secure innovation and digital transformation, provide security guidance for strategic initiatives and new capabilities, and support operational resilience and business continuity
Lead security awareness and training across the organization, promoting a security-first mindset and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, resilience, and risk awareness
Manage technology vendor and third-party security assessments while maintaining effective relationships with security vendors, managed security service providers, industry and regulatory bodies, external advisors, and peer security leaders within the financial services industry

What you’ll bring:

Deep technical knowledge of enterprise security architecture, including zero trust, network segmentation, secure-by-design principles, defence-in-depth, secure software development, DevSecOps, application security testing, and API security
Strong understanding of hybrid and multi-cloud environments, cloud security posture management, and security across SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS platforms, with the ability to assess the security implications of core insurance and wealth platforms, legacy systems, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions
Extensive experience with SIEM, endpoint detection and response, and 24x7 security monitoring models, including managed security service providers, along with vulnerability and patch management, threat intelligence, penetration testing, and red/purple team practices
Proven ability to lead cyber incident response, crisis management, forensics, and recovery activities, including ransomware and third-party breach scenarios, with a strong understanding of disaster recovery, backup integrity, and operational resilience for critical business services
Deep knowledge of identity governance, privileged access management, multifactor authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, identity lifecycle controls, access certification, segregation of duties, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud and legacy environments
Strong knowledge of data discovery and classification, data loss prevention, encryption in transit and at rest, and cryptographic key, certificate, and secrets management, including controls protecting sensitive information shared with third parties or used by AI-enabled solutions
Demonstrated ability to challenge security designs and assessment findings, validate control effectiveness through technical evidence, and prioritize remediation based on exploitability, risk, and business impact
Experience evaluating security technologies and service providers for effectiveness, integration, operational complexity, and total cost of ownership, with the ability to translate technical gaps into prioritized security roadmaps with measurable outcomes, funding requirements, and the skills and resources required for delivery

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

If you’re selected to move forward, our Talent Acquisition team will walk you through all the details of our total rewards program, so you know exactly what’s included. This position is open and we are excited to find the right person to join our team. Your base pay will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and education.

jobs.title: Director, AI Governance & Enablement
jobs.description:
We are hiring a Director, AI Governance & Enablement on behalf of a well-established organization in Mississauga.

In your new role as a Director, AI Governance & Enablement, you will be accountable for operating and advancing company’s enterprise AI practice. The role exists to help the organization adopt AI safely, practically, and at scale by combining governance discipline with education, advisory support, and pragmatic implementation guidance. It is not a research or data science role.

You will operate the governance processes that determine how AI is introduced into day-to-day work, help departments identify and prioritize valuable AI use cases, and ensure AI systems are deployed responsibly as they become more multimodal, more connected to enterprise data, and more capable of influencing decisions, workflows, and user behaviour. The role also serves as AI expertise-as-a-service function, working across corporate departments, FASTech, Service Management & Automation, Business Analysis & Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics, Privacy, Cybersecurity, and enterprise applications so that AI-enabled solutions are useful, explainable, governable, and aligned to operational realities.

The position has no direct reports. Authority is exercised through ownership of enterprise AI governance processes, leadership of the AI enablement program portfolio, management of third-party AI partner relationships, and cross-functional influence rather than direct supervision. The role owns the working relationship with external AI platform providers, training partners, and advisory firms — holding them to company’s governance, privacy, and security expectations, and leveraging them to extend internal AI education and enablement capacity. Governance framework design, risk-tier definitions, and final approval authority for higher-risk AI initiatives rest with the Director, Innovation & Technology Enablement; this role recommends, operates, and enforces.

Key Accountabilities

Enterprise AI Governance

Recommend, maintain, and continuously improve AI governance framework, standards, guardrails, and acceptable-use practices in alignment with legal, privacy, security, and risk requirements, escalating framework changes to the Director for approval.
Apply and document practical controls for responsible AI use, including human accountability, override mechanisms, confidence thresholds, auditability, data handling expectations, and documentation standards.
Operate the AI intake and review process end to end — triage, assessment, and recommendation on appropriateness, value, risk, explainability, and organizational readiness.
Apply established risk classification and approval paths, distinguishing between low-risk productivity uses, operational decision support, and higher-risk use cases, and route initiatives above the defined threshold to the Director for decision.
Partner with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and enterprise technology leaders to ensure AI-enabled solutions meet policy, compliance, and audit expectations.
Define and apply governance expectations for third-party AI providers and partners, including data handling, model transparency, sub-processor disclosure, and alignment to company’s privacy and security requirements, working with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and Procurement.

AI Education & Organizational Readiness

Design and deliver role-based AI education, awareness, and training programs for leaders, practitioners, and end users.
Create and maintain practical playbooks, templates, examples, and decision guides that help teams use AI effectively and responsibly.
Promote AI literacy across the organization by translating technical concepts into plain-language guidance and actionable practices.
Support leaders in understanding the opportunities and risks of multimodal AI, connected AI, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted decision support.
Track adoption, usage patterns, and learning outcomes to refine enablement programs and improve organizational readiness.
Manage third-party training and enablement partners, including scope, delivery quality, and alignment of externally sourced content to Chartwell’s AI standards and governance expectations.

AI Expertise-as-a-Service (Advisory)

Provide advisory support to corporate departments on AI opportunities, use-case framing, vendor and tool evaluation, and solution options.
Help teams convert ambiguous problems into clear AI and automation use cases with defined objectives, constraints, risks, and success measures.
Support business and technology teams during design and implementation with practical guidance on model and tool selection, workflow design, prompting patterns, and integration considerations.
Act as a trusted internal partner who helps departments move from experimentation to controlled, business-aligned AI adoption.
Contribute expert guidance to FASTech and other delivery teams so that AI-enabled solutions remain practical, supportable, and aligned with enterprise standards.

Safeguarding the Organization as AI Evolves

Develop guidance and control patterns for AI systems that use text, images, documents, screenshots, voice, and other multimodal inputs or outputs.
Apply governance to AI systems connected to enterprise data sources, documents, communications, applications, and external research tools.
Assess and mitigate risks related to hallucinations, model drift, privacy invasion, data leakage, bias, impersonation, surveillance, over-reliance, and unsafe automation.
Recommend boundaries for where AI may assist versus where decisions must remain deterministic or human-owned, especially for safety, compliance, financial approvals, and resident-impacting decisions.
Provide guidance on the safe use of AI as an assistant, coach, or decision-support tool, including controls to prevent manipulation, inappropriate inference, or hidden monitoring behaviours.

Program Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Lead the AI enablement program portfolio, including planning, sequencing, stakeholder coordination, and delivery tracking against committed outcomes.
Work closely with FASTech, Service Management & Automation, Business Analysis & Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics, Cybersecurity, enterprise applications, and business leaders to align AI adoption with business priorities.
Own the ongoing working relationship with third-party AI platform providers, advisory firms, and education partners, including roadmap awareness, escalation paths, and periodic performance and risk review.
Maintain the enterprise register of approved AI use cases, tools, integrations, risks, and realized outcomes.
Prepare executive reporting on AI pipeline, enablement activities, governance findings, adoption levels, and realized value for presentation by the Director.
Identify recurring themes, risks, and opportunities across departments and recommend pragmatic improvements to AI operating model.

Qualifications

Education

Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Data, Information Systems, Business, Risk, Privacy, or a related discipline is preferred.
Demonstrated and credible expertise in AI governance, responsible AI, and enterprise AI enablement will be strongly considered in lieu of a formal degree.
Coursework, certifications, or professional development in AI governance, privacy, risk, responsible AI, or change management are assets.

Experience

8+ years of progressive professional experience in technology, digital transformation, technology advisory, or a closely related field.
5+ years of combined, demonstrable experience across AI governance, AI adoption and enablement, people enablement and training, and hands-on AI solution development.
Demonstrated experience establishing or operating governance, standards, or policy controls for enterprise technology or AI adoption.
Experience designing and delivering training, communications, and change readiness programs for technology adoption.
Practical working experience with large language models, copilots, AI agents, multimodal AI, and AI systems connected to enterprise data and workflows, including hands-on prototyping or solution build.
Experience leading programs or workstreams to delivery without direct authority over contributors.
Experience operating in a mid-sized, decentralized, multi-site environment is an asset; exposure to seniors housing, real estate, healthcare delivery, retail, or hospitality operations is an asset.

Skills & Abilities

Communication:
Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to translate technical concepts into clear guidance for business leaders and end users.
Influence & Facilitation:
Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and influence skills across functions and levels, including the ability to hold a governance position under pressure while maintaining constructive working relationships.
Risk Judgement:
Pragmatic risk management mindset with the ability to balance innovation with restraint.
Technology Assessment:
Ability to assess emerging AI capabilities and convert them into practical organizational guidance and standards.
Program Discipline:
Structured approach to planning, documentation, and delivery tracking so that enablement commitments are measurable and auditable.

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix

Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe?

Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars.

En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil
, du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien?

Partenariat exécutif et gouvernance du portefeuille
Leadership opérationnel: Agir à titre de principal leader opérationnel des technologies numériques au Canada, en gérant les priorités concurrentes et en favorisant une étroite harmonisation entre les différentes unités d’affaires et régions géographiques.
Maturité du PMO: Définir et mettre en œuvre une stratégie pluriannuelle pour le PMO, en établissant des modèles opérationnels robustes, des cadres de gouvernance et des indicateurs de performance favorisant une exécution cohérente du portefeuille.
Stratégie d’investissement: Collaborer avec la direction pour identifier, prioriser et gérer l’allocation des fonds aux investissements technologiques stratégiques, tout en maintenant une feuille de route régionale de transformation numérique.
Visibilité exécutive: Mettre en place des tableaux de bord automatisés et des systèmes de gestion au sein de l’écosystème régional de gestion de portefeuille de projets (PPM), afin de fournir à la direction une visibilité en temps réel sur la santé du portefeuille, les risques et les résultats d’affaires.
Gestion et exécution de programmes complexes

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

Role Summary

The Director, Non-Financial Risk Assessment Programs leads how Capital Markets carries out BMO's main non-financial risk identification and assessment programs: PRC (Process, Risk & Control) and Risk ID inventories and RCSA (Risk & Control Self-Assessment) and RCRAs (Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment). The Director is the main point of coordination between the first line (1LOD) Business Control teams and the second line (2LOD) enterprise program owners. They make sure assessments are accurate, defensible, delivered on time, and meet ONFR and ECP requirements.

The Director brings a deep understanding of how risks, controls, processes, products, business units and legal entities connect across Capital Markets. They advocate with enterprise program owners for structures and methodologies that fit the business. The role improves inventory quality, makes execution consistent across business units (BUs), reduces the workload on Business Controls and Business Units and improves portfolio level assessments

Key Accountabilities

Inventory governance and PRC management
Own year-round governance and data-quality oversight of BU PRC inventories (products and services, internal activities, processes, specific risks and controls).
Lead the annual PRC Inventory Confirmation.
Manage organizational and ownership changes, including BU realignments, lift-and-shifts, new inventory builds, MCC/ME updates and inventory rationalization.
Monitor inventory health through Risk Mart and Power BI. Find missing attributes, linkages and data-quality issues, then drive remediation and escalate unresolved gaps.
Make sure applicable Master Common Controls (MCCs) and shared controls are adopted correctly in BU control inventories, including SOX designations.
Capital Markets risk structure and cross-program linkages
Act as the authoritative interpreter of PRC, RCSA, RCRA for Capital Markets.
Act as Capital Markets' expert on how products and services, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities connect, and keep that view current as the business and organization change.
Advocate with the enterprise program owner for the data structure, taxonomy and linkage design that best fits Capital Markets, including how KRIs, Issues and Events connect to PRC risk and control records.
Give business requirements and practical input on changes to the GRCE data model, workflow and future-state integration, including aggregation at the Legal Entity level.
Make sure Capital Markets inventories apply the agreed linkage standards consistently. This includes keeping Issues linked to Key Controls complete and accurate
Find structural gaps or misalignments, such as missing, orphaned or inconsistent linkages, and bring them to the program owner with recommended fixes.
Use the linked data to support RCSA residual risk ratings, overrides and Targeted Risk Evaluations (TREs) with evidence, and to show where control weaknesses, KRI breaches and loss events cluster.
Risk assessment execution (RCSA and RCRA)
Lead the PRC/RCSA/RCRA Annual Plan.
Oversee risk categorization (key vs. non-key) and ensure assessments are right sized taking a risk based approach.
Oversee reviews of TREs, including inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk, overrides and rationales. Ensure High Residual Risk ratings have corrective actions to improve control effectiveness.
Lead RCRA execution and work with Business Regulatory Control teams to maintain and accurate inventory of risk evaluation points (REPs). Reconcile RCRA results with the regulatory and privacy TREs in the RCSA so regulatory compliance risk feeds into the BU risk profile.
Manage slippage and deferral requests, and exception and exemption requests, in line with Directive requirements.
Coordinate Effective Challenge from Operational Risk Officers (OROs), Risk Specialty Areas (RSAs), Enterprise Control Functions (ECFs) and other programs. Track comments, how they're resolved, and due dates.
Advocacy with 2LOD program owners
Act as Capital Markets' lead advocate with the 2LOD program owners (ONFR, ECP and Regulatory Compliance, and Risk Specialty Areas). Represent the business's interests in methodology, Policy, Standard & Procedure changes.
Influence program design so requirements suit Capital Markets' products, trading activities and legal entity structure and aid towards reducing risk.
Negotiate realistic timelines, scope and sequencing for program deliverables. Prepare well- supported rationale for exceptions, exemptions or alternative approaches when they're justified.
Bring the business's perspective, practical constraints and lessons learned to enterprise working groups and consultations. Share upcoming program changes with Director, Risk Programs for inclusion in broader communications across Capital Markets.
Build trusted, credible relationships with 2LOD so issues are resolved collaboratively and escalated only when needed.
Reporting and executive enablement
Produce AE summary materials and approval packages, and keep approval evidence in GRCE.
Provide risk profile insights and committee reporting (for example, VRC).
Continuous improvement and future-state capability
Lead improvements to methodology, process, reporting and systems with ONFR. Standardize tools, templates and procedures.
Represent Capital Markets in working groups, user acceptance testing (UAT) and platform evaluations to shape GRCE and future assessment capabilities.
People leadership
Lead, develop and set priorities for team members and Business Control teams across concurrent assessment cycles.
Build a culture of accountability, data quality and practical, business-friendly risk partnership.

Key relationships

1LOD: Business Controls, Risk Domain Leads, Business Unit Leads, Accountable Executives, Operational Resilience & Risk Programs, Portfolio Analytics, Capital Markets Assurance Role, Enterprise Control Functions
2LOD: ONFR and ECP program & methodology owners, OROs, RSAs, Regulatory Compliance and Privacy

Qualifications

10+ years in operational or non-financial risk, risk and control self-assessment, or governance at a large financial institution, including people leadership. Capital Markets experience strongly preferred.
Deep understanding of how Capital Markets products, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities relate, and the ability to turn that into clear structural requirements for enterprise program owners.
Deep knowledge of the three lines of defence model, risk and control taxonomies, residual risk methods and Effective Challenge.
Proven ability to influence and negotiate with 2LOD and enterprise program owners, representing business interests credibly and constructively.
Hands-on experience with a GRC platform (Archer preferred) and with data and reporting tools (Power BI, Risk Mart).
Track record of leading enterprise programs on regulatory deadlines and producing audit- ready, AE-ready and committee-ready materials.
Strong judgment and executive presence, and the ability to escalate issues diplomatically with senior stakeholders.

This is the place for purpose-driven individuals ready to deliver impactful leadership every day.

About The Role

As the Director of Market Risk Oversight & Counterparty Credit Risk
, you will provide strategic direction, leadership, and operational success over ATB’s traded financial risks. In an environment where ATB Capital Markets is scaling into a full-service broker, this leadership role bridges the gap between sophisticated trading activities and robust institutional risk boundaries.

You will manage a dedicated team of risk professionals and act as a senior expert advisor across the second line of defense. This role transforms risk oversight from flat compliance into a proactive, data-driven vertical that delivers deep analytical insights, robust independent challenges, and strategic protection of the firm’s bottom line.

Accountabilities

Strategic Leadership & Governance

Develop and execute the long-term vision, strategy, and operating standards for the Trade Floor Market Risk Oversight and Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) pillars.
Own, maintain, and spearhead limit reviews and calibrations, collaborating with risk and front office stakeholders to ensure risk limits are aligned with risk appetite and business strategy.
Be the subject matter expert for annual and intra-cycle updates of the Board-level Market Risk Management Policy and accompanying Frameworks.
Act as a core member and senior presenter at the Market Risk Oversight Committee (MROC), presenting key market and counterparty credit risk insights and effectively escalating risk postures to the Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO).
Lead the review and implementation of new traded products via the New Initiative Risk Assessment Process (NIRAP) to safely onboard new capital market instruments and product lines.
Design, implement, and execute a rigorous 2nd line control framework to continuously validate market risk and counterparty credit risk models via systematic backtesting.

Market Risk Oversight & Analytics

Oversee independent daily monitoring and granular analysis of desk-level trading risks across traded securities and derivatives products (including Fixed Income, Interest Rates, Foreign Exchange, Equities, and Commodities).
Ensure absolute integrity of end-of-day (EOD) and intra-day risk reporting metrics, including Value-at-Risk (VaR), Stressed VaR (SVaR), sensitivities/Greeks (DV01, CS01), and Notional limits.
Direct real-time limit excess management and breach escalation protocols across first and second lines of defense.
Drive the end-to-end framework for ensuring that market risk models, measurements, and risk engines are structurally sound, comprehensive, and accurate.
Establish robust processes and controls to guarantee that all risk factors—specifically complex nuances like basis risk (including tenor, currency, and index basis mismatches), volatility smiles, and correlation breakdowns—are fully captured, mapped, and measured
Lead the development and enhancement of trade floor and counterparty credit risk reporting and analytics to foster proactive risk management.
Strengthen and maintain the robustness of market risk frameworks by effectively identifying and capturing risks across unique, complex, and bespoke business lines (e.g., equity bought deals, off-market trades)

Counterparty Credit Risk Oversight

Formulate and enforce the strategic 2nd line framework for all traded credit exposures, including Potential Future Exposure (PFE) profiles, single name issuer risk and settlement risk.
Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and rigorous governance of model inputs feeding into counterparty credit risk engines, including credit curve mappings, ensuring that Potential Future Exposure (PFE) model parameters are mathematically sound and reflective of current market dynamics
Monitor portfolio concentrations and counterparty credit updates across Issuer Risk, Repo, Derivatives, and Collateral frameworks.
Strengthen Counterparty Credit Risk policies & frameworks by aligning with industry and regulatory best practices.

Required Qualifications

Skills, experience & requirements

A University degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Financial Engineering, or a highly quantitative discipline.
8+ years of progressive experience working within financial markets in either a 1st line (Front Office/Execution) or 2nd line (Risk Management) financial risk role.
Professional certifications such as FRM, CFA, or PRMIA are a strong asset.

Core Technical Skills

Mastered expertise in multi-asset Capital Markets financial instruments (FICC derivatives, equities, repo, debt capital markets).
Advanced understanding of derivative pricing, risk-neutral and real-world simulation modeling frameworks, Monte Carlo engines, and volatility skews/smiles.
In-depth practical knowledge of risk systems, specifically Murex and Bloomberg (MARS/TOMS).
Quantitative data proficiency utilizing tools like Python, SQL, and Google BigQuery (DEEP architecture).

Leadership & Interpersonal Attributes

Proven people leader capable of mentoring high-performing analysts and managers, cultivating technical excellence, and fostering a collaborative, psychological safe culture.
Elite stakeholder management and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to deliver a credible, robust challenge to first-line business line heads and traders.

new_jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
new_jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), you’ll provide strategic and operational leadership for Equitable’s enterprise information security program, protecting our information assets, technology infrastructure, applications, data, and digital capabilities while enabling business growth and innovation. You’ll define and execute our cyber security strategy, ensuring effective security controls, processes, and practices are embedded across technology and business operations. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, you’ll lead the continued development of a resilient, risk-aware security culture while ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and recognized security frameworks.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

Reports To:
Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer

Department:
Information Technology

Term:
Permanent Full-Time

What you’ll do:

Serve as a senior technology leader and trusted advisor to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer and Executive Team on cyber security, significant incidents, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security program developments
Develop and execute the enterprise cyber security strategy, roadmap, budget, and investment priorities aligned with business and technology objectives, including anticipating and mitigating risks associated with AI-enabled threats and vulnerabilities
Establish and maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, controls, metrics, and performance indicators, driving continuous improvement in the organization’s security capabilities and maturity
Lead security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability management, cyber resilience, incident response, recovery, post-incident remediation, and the oversight of security service providers and critical technology assets
Oversee security architecture, identity and access management, data protection, cloud and endpoint security, ensuring appropriate controls are integrated into technology solutions, projects, and business processes
Partner with business and technology leaders to enable secure innovation and digital transformation, provide security guidance for strategic initiatives and new capabilities, and support operational resilience and business continuity
Lead security awareness and training across the organization, promoting a security-first mindset and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, resilience, and risk awareness
Manage technology vendor and third-party security assessments while maintaining effective relationships with security vendors, managed security service providers, industry and regulatory bodies, external advisors, and peer security leaders within the financial services industry

What you’ll bring:

Deep technical knowledge of enterprise security architecture, including zero trust, network segmentation, secure-by-design principles, defence-in-depth, secure software development, DevSecOps, application security testing, and API security
Strong understanding of hybrid and multi-cloud environments, cloud security posture management, and security across SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS platforms, with the ability to assess the security implications of core insurance and wealth platforms, legacy systems, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions
Extensive experience with SIEM, endpoint detection and response, and 24x7 security monitoring models, including managed security service providers, along with vulnerability and patch management, threat intelligence, penetration testing, and red/purple team practices
Proven ability to lead cyber incident response, crisis management, forensics, and recovery activities, including ransomware and third-party breach scenarios, with a strong understanding of disaster recovery, backup integrity, and operational resilience for critical business services
Deep knowledge of identity governance, privileged access management, multifactor authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, identity lifecycle controls, access certification, segregation of duties, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud and legacy environments
Strong knowledge of data discovery and classification, data loss prevention, encryption in transit and at rest, and cryptographic key, certificate, and secrets management, including controls protecting sensitive information shared with third parties or used by AI-enabled solutions
Demonstrated ability to challenge security designs and assessment findings, validate control effectiveness through technical evidence, and prioritize remediation based on exploitability, risk, and business impact
Experience evaluating security technologies and service providers for effectiveness, integration, operational complexity, and total cost of ownership, with the ability to translate technical gaps into prioritized security roadmaps with measurable outcomes, funding requirements, and the skills and resources required for delivery

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

If you’re selected to move forward, our Talent Acquisition team will walk you through all the details of our total rewards program, so you know exactly what’s included. This position is open and we are excited to find the right person to join our team. Your base pay will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and education.

JOB DESCRIPTION

BGIS is a leading provider of customized facility management and real estate services. With a combined team of over 10,000 professionals worldwide, we relentlessly focus on enabling innovation through the services we deliver. We actively seek new opportunities that drive innovation for our clients’ businesses. Globally, we manager over 320 million square feet of client portfolios across 30,000+ locations in North America, Europe, Middle East, Australia, and Asia. For further information, visit www.bgis.com .

OUR CULTURE

At BGIS, our culture is built on three foundational pillars:

Culture of Care: We deeply care for each other, our clients, partners, and the communities we serve.
High Performing Teams: We go Above and Beyond to deliver exceptional services. INTEGRITY, OWNERSHIP, RESPONSIVENESS, INITIATION, VISIBILITY, DRIVE, and INTEGRATION are core to high performance.

is accountable for operations, financial management and meeting service delivery obligations in a specified Geographical region that includes several facilities, employees and clients.  This role is expected to understand, coach and train the team in all regulatory and client requirements.  In addition, this role is also responsible for contributing to strategic and account management plans and objectives and people leadership. 

This role will work in collaboration with all key BGIS departments to ensure full support of all activities and play a key role in our INTEGRATED approach to operating buildings.   

Opportunities for Development:  

At BGIS we are committed to the development of our people – offering them opportunities to learn and grow into various roles.  Success in the role offers Team Members the opportunity to explore various roles – some include:  

On Account and expanded Operational Leadership
Facility Management Office roles to support accounts,
Project Management leadership roles to lead and execute projects

Health, Safety, Environment & Security

Follow and apply all Health and Safety and Emergency Response, aligned with both BGIS and Client expectations.to ensure safety of all employees and building occupants. 
Work in collaboration with BGIS Health Safety and Environment Teams for support and direction on key programs to emphasize Safety Culture 
Accountable for meeting all internal and external health, safety, environment and security-related requirements 
Accountable for the safe delivery of all work performed  

Account Management

Continuously engages clients in discussions to understand and anticipate needs, identify and recommend additional services   
Provides input and contributes to the development and execution of strategic account expansion plans 
Recommends additional pull-through services 
Participates in and contributes to quarterly business reviews

Adherence to Contract Specific MSA (Master Service Agreement)

Responsible for results and action plans related to the Likely to Recommend Survey.  

Client Relationship Management

Accountable for achieving client satisfaction objectives for the assigned region(s) 
Accountable for developing and maintaining effective relationships with clients, managing client expectations 
Position level of client representatives with whom this position typically interacts with include those at the senior management level 
Acts as the focal point of escalation for issues pertaining to facilities within assigned region(s) 

Region/Portfolio Budget Development & Management

Assume financial responsibility for facility operations, including budget management. 
In partnership with finance, responsible for the development of budgets (O&M, Transaction, capital projects and rent), and be able to support and explain approach to the client and the account team.  
Using financial reports, perform monthly budget, analyze and re-forecast allocations as necessary. 
Meet annual targets as per contractual performance and client financial targets / indicators. 
Identify cost-saving opportunities and develop strategies to maximize financial resources. 
Track and report on budget positive or negative trends performance regularly 
Participates in, provides recommendations, and contributes to continuous improvement projects to achieve efficiency gains and cost savings 

Portfolio Management

Accountable for operations management for the portfolio of facilities within the assigned region(s) 
Leads the operations and maintenance activities of a portfolio of facilities along with the execution of the portfolio’s programs 
Oversees the completion and submission of capital plans

Provides input into strategic plans   
Collaborates with relevant stakeholders to optimize facilities within assigned region(s) and continuously create value for the client.

Monitor work order progress and ensure tasks are completed within established timelines. 
Work with Account Governance Teams to maintain accurate records of work orders and associated costs. 
Streamline and manage work order processes to optimize efficiency. 
Prioritize and assign work orders based on urgency and impact on facility operations. 
Accountable for meeting all service obligations for the assigned region(s) 
Oversees the delivery of all service obligations 
Accountable for meeting established metrics/key performance indicators.  Leads the operations team in the development and implementation of action plans to remediate gaps, where applicable, to ensure objectives are met. 
Accountable for ensuring compliance to all legislated, corporate and industry-related requirements and guidelines including but not limited to environmental, health and safety, and building standard requirements 

Risk Management, Emergency Preparedness and Business Continuity Planning and Execution

Accountable for safeguarding the client against emergencies and risks by ensuring emergency preparedness, risk management, disaster recovery and business continuity plans are developed and that relevant stakeholders are trained to ensure proper execution 
Oversight and engagement in Emergency Management 

Regulatory Compliance

Accountable for ensuring all regulatory compliance requirements have been met and all related documentation are created and maintained 
Ensure compliance with corporate and legislated policies, procedures, practices and guidelines related to environmental, building code and issues by applying cursory knowledge of legislation related to these areas 

Project Management

Accountable for on-time, on-budget and quality delivery of facility management projects for the assigned region(s) 
Collaborates with clients and internal stakeholders to identify project opportunities and priorities, develop and implement projects 
Oversees the development and execution of project plans for portfolios within assigned region(s) 

Procurement

With Support from BGIS Strategic Sourcing and Vendor Management Leadership – follow BGIS Vendor Performance and Relationship Management Program protocols  
Collaborates with Procurement and Supply Chain Administration teams to source and qualify vendors, source and procure goods and services. 

Continuous Improvement

Collaborates with stakeholders and contributes to efficiency gains   through activities including but not limited to identifying and implementing best practices; reviewing, refining and/or developing, implementing processes, technologies and sustainable practices, and leveraging self-perform wherever possible.  Implements related enhancements for the assigned region(s) 

Leadership and Recognition

Accountable for employee-oriented activities including but not limited to employee engagement, development and performance management, hiring and retention, compensation recommendations 
Employee Satisfaction Scores and employee recognition (development and implementation of action plans to improve ESAT scores) 
Day to day support and team oversight/management 

Collaboration with BGIS Self Perform Teams delivering Best Quality Services to Buildings 

Work in collaboration with BGIS teams in Janitorial, Project Management and TechnicalServices or any other areas where work is directly performed by BGIS to maximize efficiency and the best customer service in the buildings / portfolios  
Work together with these teams to ensure work is completed 

Technology to Support your Success.

Mentor staff in vendor management and the effective use of technology for vendor relationships. 
Provide guidance to team members on the effective use of technology for financial management and career progression. 
Other duties as assigned

Community college diploma preferably in business administration
More than 10 years of facility management work experience
Highly skilled at account management
Highly skilled at facility operations management
Highly skilled at client relationship management with demonstrated ability in building and managing relationships with client representatives at the senior management level
Highly skilled at managing service delivery and meeting service delivery obligations
Skilled at managing budgets
Fully developed communication, influence, persuasion and negotiation skills
High degree of client service orientation and sense of urgency
Highly skilled at leading and engaging a team of individuals

Possesses a sustainability mindset and seeks to incorporate sustainable practices within assigned portfolio where possible

Possesses a continuous improvement and quality mindset along with a desire to continuously seek and incorporate innovative practices and technologies in order to deliver value to the client
